title: Transformer working principle and equivalent circuit
content: The working principle of a transformer is based on electromagnetic induction: the primary current produces magnetic flux, and an electromotive force is induced on the secondary side. Derivation of the equivalent circuit: at no load, it is equivalent to the magnetizing reactance Xm in parallel with the core-loss resistance Rm; at load, the leakage reactances X1, X2 and winding resistances R1, R2 are considered. Draw the T-type equivalent circuit: on the left, the primary leakage reactance is in series with the resistance; in the middle, the magnetizing branch is in parallel; on the right, the secondary leakage reactance and series resistance are referred to the primary side. The voltage ratio is k=N1/N2.

title: Master Li explains: troubleshooting transformer differential protection.
content:
1. Check whether the current transformer polarity is correct and the differential circuit wiring is correct.
2. Measure the currents on each side of the differential relay and calculate the unbalanced current.
3. If the differential protection operates, check the fault recording and analyze the waveform characteristics.
4. Check whether the DC power supply voltage is normal and whether the relay's internal contacts are in good condition.
5. Recheck the CT ratio and connection group to rule out wiring errors.
